privacy.title: Privacy Notice
privacy.intro: RecompAchievements is a community project. This notice explains what we collect when you sign up for the alpha or create an account, why, and how to remove it.

sections.title: What We Collect
sections.body: Alpha sign-up: your email address, nickname, the platforms you play on, the recomps you mention, the site language you used, and when you agreed to this notice and confirmed your email. Account: your username, email address (once you confirm it), a securely hashed password if you set one, the site language, and, if you sign in with Discord or GitHub, that platform’s account ID (and its email, only when the platform says it’s verified and you use it for your account). We also record when your account was created and last changed, when you were last active, and whether it’s enabled. Your public profile shows your username, when you joined, the day you were last active (never the time), and comments on your wall; your achievement progress will be public too. Your email and connected platforms are never shown. We don’t store your IP address.

sections.title: Comments
sections.body: Comments you post on a player’s wall or a game page are public and stored until you delete them, your account is deleted, or we remove them. A wall’s owner can also delete comments on their wall. Forum posts are written by the RecompAchievements team and show the author’s username.

sections.title: Profile Photos and Moderation
sections.body: If you upload a profile photo, it’s public. We store only a resized copy without its metadata, such as location, and we record when you confirmed you may use it. Your photo is deleted when you remove or replace it, when moderators remove it, or when your account is disabled. If you report content, we keep your report and share it only with moderators. We also keep a record of moderation decisions; text kept as evidence is erased after 90 days, except where the law requires us to keep it, such as serious illegal content.

sections.title: Why
sections.body: To run the alpha and your account: confirm your email, sign you in, keep your account secure, send account emails you ask for (confirmation and password links) or that protect you (a password change or a newly connected platform), and, later, track your achievements. We don’t sell or share your data, and we don’t send marketing emails.

sections.title: Where It’s Kept
sections.body: In our database at our hosting provider. Emails are sent through our email delivery provider. Both act only on our instructions. If you choose Discord or GitHub, they tell us who you are when you sign in; we never receive your password there.

sections.title: Bot Protection
sections.body: Before you sign up or ask for a password link, a short check in your browser confirms you’re a person, not an automated script. It’s run by a security service that sees only technical information about your browser and connection, used solely for this check. We don’t receive or store it.

sections.title: How Long
sections.body: Unconfirmed alpha sign-ups are deleted automatically 7 days after the link is sent; confirmed ones are kept until the alpha ends, then deleted unless you create an account. Accounts are kept until you ask us to delete them. Registrations never confirmed are deleted once their link expires (24 hours), and sign-in sessions end after 30 days without use.

sections.title: Cookies
sections.body: No tracking or advertising cookies. Functional cookies only: NEXT_LOCALE remembers the language you chose; when you sign in, one cookie keeps you signed in; and short-lived ones (15 minutes) hold a Discord or GitHub sign-in while it’s in progress.

sections.title: Your Rights
sections.body: You can ask to see, correct, or delete your data or your account at any time by writing to {email}.

contentPolicy.metaDescription: What RecompAchievements hosts, where game images come from, and how rights holders can request removal.
contentPolicy.title: Content Policy
contentPolicy.intro: RecompAchievements is a community project that tracks achievements for recomps and native PC ports. This page explains what we host and how to ask us to remove something.

sections.title: What We Don’t Host
sections.body: No games, ROMs, disc images, recompiled executables, or game files of any kind. Every recomp needs your own legally obtained copy of the original game, and downloads come only from each project’s own pages.

sections.title: Achievement Text
sections.body: Achievement titles and descriptions are written by us or by recomp developers. We don’t copy official trophy or achievement lists.

sections.title: Images
sections.body: We never use game logos or official trophy icons, and we don’t store game art on our servers. Covers, backgrounds, and icons come from SteamGridDB, chosen by hand or picked from its top-rated images, and loaded from its servers, and are shown only to identify each game. Every image is credited on its game page with the artist and a link to its SteamGridDB page. Games without art get generated artwork.

sections.title: Trademarks
sections.body: Game and platform names are trademarks of their owners and are used only to identify the games. RecompAchievements is not affiliated with or endorsed by any game publisher, platform holder, or recomp developer unless stated.

sections.title: Player Comments
sections.body: Players are responsible for the comments they post on profile walls and game pages. A comment’s author can delete it, and so can a wall’s owner. To report abusive or infringing comments, use the Report button or write to {email}.

sections.title: Player Photos
sections.body: Profile photos are uploaded by players, who confirm they may use them. We can’t review every image in advance. To report one, use the Report button or write to {email}.

sections.title: Removal Requests
sections.body: If you hold rights to something shown on this site and want it removed, email {email} with a link to the page and what you’d like removed. We review every request and remove content within 5 business days when the request is valid.

rules.metaDescription: What you can post on RecompAchievements, how copyright complaints work, and what happens when rules are broken.
rules.title: Community Rules
rules.intro: These rules apply to everything players post on RecompAchievements, including usernames, profile photos, and comments.

sections.title: Not Allowed
sections.body: No nudity or sexual content, graphic violence or gore, hate or discrimination, harassment or threats, other people’s private information, spam, or anything illegal. Content that sexualizes minors is never allowed; we remove it, disable the account, and report it to the authorities.

sections.title: Profile Photos
sections.body: By uploading a photo, you confirm that you own it or have the right to use it, and that it follows these rules. Photos are public as soon as you save them. You can replace or remove yours at any time in your account settings.

sections.title: Copyright
sections.body: Only post what you’re allowed to use. We can’t review every image in advance, so rights holders can ask us to remove content by emailing {email} with a link to it, what they own, and how to contact them. We remove content within 5 business days when a request is valid. Accounts that repeatedly infringe are disabled.

sections.title: Reporting
sections.body: If you’re signed in, use the Report button on a profile, photo, or comment. You can also write to {email}. Moderators review reports, and we don’t tell the reported player who sent them.

sections.title: What Moderators Can Do
sections.body: Moderators can remove content, mute an account (it can’t post or change its photo, but it can still earn achievements), or disable it. We tell you the reason by email, unless the law or the safety of others prevents it.

sections.title: Appeals
sections.body: If you think a decision was wrong, write to {email} with your username and why. A person will review it.
